docs.text: Supported queries and validation ¶ The generator compiles a JSON results URL from an lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. Jinja2 emits a pygeofilter evaluator with embedded validation definitions; invoke expands the original OpenSearch URL template and sends that URL through requests . The generated module runs without the osdd2pygeofilter package, Jinja2, or lxml. Regenerate it to pick up changes to validation rules. Only advertised placeholders are exposed as properties. Query names may differ from those properties: q={searchTerms} maps searchTerms to q . CQL2 translation ¶ Expression Translation Scalar equality, including reversed operands Parameter assignment AND Combine assignments; reject conflicts EO numeric/date < , <= , > , >= EO one-sided interval notation EO numeric/date BETWEEN / IN Inclusive interval / set notation Conjunction of EO intervals Intersect bounds; reject an empty intersection S_INTERSECTS on a geo:geometry property Exact WKT and geo:relation=intersects when advertised Dates and timestamps use ISO serialization; booleans use true or false . Identical assignments are deduplicated. Spatial predicates never approximate a geometry by its bounding box. A bounding box can be assigned directly to the advertised geo:box property. OpenSearch descriptions do not define a universal translation for arbitrary CQL2. OR , NOT , null predicates, arithmetic, functions, general temporal predicates, and comparisons on parameters without an EO range contract fail explicitly. Time filters can assign RFC 3339 values to time:start and time:end ; these are overlap search bounds, not a general implementation of CQL2 temporal relations. Distinct scalar/set assignments to the same parameter are rejected, including mixed scalar/interval conjunctions. Validation ¶ Invocation validates the complete parameter set, including defaults and fixed values, before sending a request. Evaluation logs warnings for unlisted option values. Contract Checks OpenSearch 1.1 Required placeholders, integer pagination, URL offsets, declared languages and encodings Parameter extension Required occurrence, scalar occurrence limits, patterns, inclusive/exclusive numeric or date bounds, numeric steps Geo WGS84 coordinate limits, ordered latitude bounds, antimeridian boxes, finite coordinates/radius, supported relation values, nonempty 2D WKT syntax and bounds Time RFC 3339 timestamps with timezone, calendar validity, chronological start/end order EO Numeric/date scalar, set and interval syntax, integer fields, cloud/snow percentages, specified enumerations, advertised range/set restrictions and member patterns SRU Integer counts/offsets, record packing, rendering, sort-key flags and facet-sort structure EUMETSAT/custom namespaces QName mapping and constraints advertised by the service's Parameter elements WKT checking is syntactic and dimensional; it does not perform GEOS topology validation. String parameters without standard enums or advertised constraints remain unrestricted. Unknown extension namespaces do not inherit another extension's semantics merely because their prefix or local name matches. The adapter supports declared input and output text encodings, defaulting to UTF-8. Explicit encoding parameters override declaration defaults; an HTTP response charset overrides the output-decoding fallback. Required placeholders need nonempty values. Missing optional placeholders are replaced with empty strings; surrounding URL text remains intact. No service defaults are invented. URL templates may contain path, authority, fragment, query-name, and composite query-value placeholders. The original template is preserved, including repeated query keys and fixed literals. Replacement values are percent-encoded once; existing literal escapes are not decoded and re-encoded. Missing required values, malformed placeholders, ambiguous parameter aliases, unsupported occurrence counts, and invalid parameter bindings are rejected. Expansion must produce an absolute HTTP(S) URL before a request is sent. Multiple JSON results URLs can be selected using url_index . Unknown foreign annotations are retained as metadata but do not trigger network requests or dynamic code. Advertised options ¶ Parameter Option elements suggest values; they do not establish an exhaustive enumeration. The generator preserves their submitted values as tuples in PARAMETER_OPTIONS , keyed by HTTP parameter name, and omits labels, without changing the underlying parameter type. Handlers log a WARNING immediately for each assigned value missing from its advertised options tuple, without rejecting or changing it. Repeated assignments and computed values are checked independently, before evaluation completes. Listed values and absent parameters are silent. A pattern alongside options is enforced at invocation, even for an advertised value. Unlisted values remain valid when they satisfy the parameter's other constraints. This follows the OGC EO guidance on supplying patterns when options describe only a subset of possible values. Closed enumerations require an explicit exhaustive contract; existing standard-defined enumerations, such as orbit direction, remain enforced. The generator does not infer a service-specific Enum, Literal, or schema enum from options alone. Specification sources ¶ OpenSearch 1.1 Draft 5 OGC EO extension 13-026r9 OGC Geo and Time extensions 10-032r8 OpenSearch SRU extension EUMETSAT live description The historical EUMETSAT namespace page could not be recovered from the archive: the exact-URL availability query returned no snapshot, and broader archive queries returned a temporary outage. Accordingly, EUMETSAT-specific rules are read from advertised constraints rather than claimed as a complete historical profile implementation. The live description advertises eum:elementSetName values full and brief , which are covered by regression tests.

docs.text: Install ¶ Use Python 3.11 or newer. From a local checkout of this repository, create a virtual environment and install the package: python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install . osdd2pygeofilter --help On Windows, activate the environment with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell. For development, use python -m pip install -e . instead. Installation supplies the command and its runtime dependencies, including Jinja2 and pygeofilter. If the command is not found, activate the environment where you installed the package. Continue with your first evaluator or CLI usage .

docs.text: Use the CLI ¶ Supply one OSDD source and a required destination Python file: osdd2pygeofilter OSDD --output FILE.py Remote descriptions ¶ osdd2pygeofilter https://api.eumetsat.int/data/search-products/1.0.0/os --output generated/eumetsat_evaluator.py Use an endpoint returning OpenSearch XML. The command fetches and parses the description, then generates an evaluator from its first Url with type="application/json" and a results relation ( rel="results" , also the default when omitted). There is no CLI option to select another URL; the Python API provides url_index for that purpose. Local descriptions ¶ osdd2pygeofilter ./opensearch.xml --output generated/search_evaluator.py Absolute paths and file:// URLs are also supported. Quote paths containing spaces. The destination is a file, not a directory. Missing parent directories are created and existing output is overwritten. HTTP bearer authentication ¶ Provide a bearer token through the environment: export OAUTH2_BEARER = 'your-token' osdd2pygeofilter https://example.test/opensearch.xml --output search_evaluator.py The equivalent option is --oauth2-bearer . It authenticates HTTP and HTTPS retrieval of the description. The token is not embedded in the generated module; your application handles authentication for subsequent search requests. OCI registry authentication ¶ Set OSDD_OCI_URL to your description's oci:// URL supported by the registry adapter, then supply a containers authentication file if needed: osdd2pygeofilter " $OSDD_OCI_URL " --authfile ./auth.json --output search_evaluator.py Alternatively, supply all three of OCI_HOSTNAME , OCI_USERNAME , and OCI_PASSWORD . The CLI reference describes credential-file lookup and the corresponding options. Use the generated module ¶ The CLI accepts an OSDD and generates Python code. To evaluate a CQL2 filter, import the resulting module as shown in the first evaluator walkthrough . The module returns parameter dictionaries. Generated invocation helpers validate them and execute requests using the selected URL’s declared HTTP method (GET by default). Troubleshooting ¶ Symptom What to check Command not found Activate the environment where the package is installed. Missing argument or option Supply both an OSDD source and --output FILE.py . HTTP or XML parsing error Confirm that the source returns OpenSearch XML and authentication is correct. A login page or search response is not an OSDD. Selected URL must have the results relation The first JSON results Url is used. Select a results URL through the Python API's url_index . Unsupported template Check for path placeholders, composite values, fragments, or duplicate query names. See limitations . Parameter extension binding error Each Parameter needs name/value attributes matching the URL template. Cannot write output Check permissions and supply a file path. Failures are logged with a traceback and exit status 1 . Successful generation does not guarantee that every CQL2 expression is supported or every parameter value is accepted by the remote service.

docs.text: API reference ¶ convert(service, target, *, url_index=0) accepts an lxml.etree._Element root element and a pathlib.Path . It validates and renders the evaluator before creating parent directories and replacing the output. It returns the target path. render_evaluator(service, *, url_index=0) returns the same Python source without writing it. from pathlib import Path from lxml import etree from osdd2pygeofilter.converter import convert parser = etree . XMLParser ( resolve_entities = False , load_dtd = False , no_network = True ) service = etree . parse ( "opensearch.xml" , parser ) . getroot () convert ( service , Path ( "generated_search.py" )) Only Url elements with type="application/json" and a results relation (including the default relation) are eligible. url_index selects among these URLs in document order. No requests are made during conversion. Generated API ¶ The module contains OpenSearchEvaluator(Evaluator) and these convenience APIs: from generated_search import from_cql2_text , from_cql2_json # For a template https://example.test/search?q={searchTerms}&limit={count?} query = from_cql2_text ( "searchTerms = 'ocean & ice' AND count = 10" ) assert query == { "q" : "ocean & ice" , "limit" : "10" } query = from_cql2_json ( '{"op":"=","args":[{"property":"searchTerms"},"ice"]}' ) to_opensearch(root) accepts an existing pygeofilter AST. Query conversion functions return decoded filter parameters without making a request. They accept attribute_map , mapping application property names to placeholder QNames. Each evaluation is independent. invoke(parameters, defaults=None) merges decoded defaults with supplied parameters and validates them. It expands the original URL_TEMPLATE in place and passes the resulting URL to requests.request(METHOD, url, timeout=30) with a 30-second timeout, without a separate params argument. Filter assignments override defaults; fixed template values cannot be changed. It raises for HTTP errors and returns the response's decoded JSON. invoke_from_cql2_text and invoke_from_cql2_json combine conversion and invocation: from generated_search import invoke_from_cql2_text response = invoke_from_cql2_text ( "text = 'ice'" , attribute_map = { "text" : "searchTerms" }, defaults = { "limit" : "10" }, ) URL_TEMPLATE preserves the selected OSDD Url/@template exactly as read from XML. Each {name} or {prefix:name?} occurrence is replaced with its percent-encoded value. Optional values that are absent become empty strings; required values must be supplied. Literal paths, separators, fixed query values, existing escapes, repeated keys, and fragments are preserved during expansion. The HTTP client may subsequently normalize the URL for transport and does not send fragment identifiers to the server. Whole query-value placeholders retain their query-name aliases ( q={searchTerms} uses q in the parameter dictionary). A matching Parameter declaration's name takes precedence. For path, composite, or ambiguous repeated query bindings, the placeholder QName is the default dictionary key. For example, /catalog/{eo:platform}/search/{searchTerms} accepts eo:platform and searchTerms , unless Parameter declarations give them other names. Repeated occurrences of a placeholder share a value; any required occurrence makes the value required. These are OpenSearch placeholders, not RFC 6570 expressions such as {?q,count} . At invocation, a small adapter maps OpenSearch placeholders to temporary RFC 6570 variable names. URITemplate performs the actual expansion and UTF-8 percent encoding; other input encodings use urllib.parse.quote before reserved expansion to preserve encoded escapes. URL_TEMPLATE itself stays unchanged. METHOD comes from the selected URL’s method or Parameters-extension p:method attribute and defaults to GET . Invocation sends the expanded URL with that method; it does not construct a request body. Input and output encodings use the explicit parameter value, then the first concrete InputEncoding or OutputEncoding declaration, then UTF-8. Encoding placeholders are populated with this selection when omitted. Codec aliases are accepted when they match an advertised encoding. Input encoding controls URL value percent encoding; output encoding controls JSON response decoding unless the response declares an HTTP charset, which takes precedence. Unknown codecs and input characters that cannot be encoded fail before a request is sent. Quote extension property names in CQL2 text, for example "eo:cloudCover" < 20 . Use attribute_map to expose names such as cloud_cover . The prefix must match the description's placeholder; its meaning is resolved using the XML namespace URI, including declarations scoped to a URL. The generated module requires pygeofilter , pygeoif (also a dependency of pygeofilter), requests , and uritemplate . It does not import osdd2pygeofilter , Jinja2, or lxml at runtime. The generator embeds the validation definitions from its canonical validation source alongside the Jinja2-rendered handlers. Validation fixes take effect in existing modules when you regenerate them. PARAMETER_OPTIONS maps HTTP query parameter names to tuples of suggested values, for example {"platform": ("Sentinel-1", "Sentinel-2")} . Option labels are omitted. Options alone do not restrict accepted values or imply an enum. Whenever a handler assigns a parameter value absent from its advertised tuple, it immediately emits a WARNING log record. Listed values, absent parameters, and parameters without options produce no warning. Comparison uses the complete decoded value, including any range, set, or sort syntax. Repeated assignments are checked separately. Computed interval intersections and spatial relation assignments are also checked; copying already checked values while merging predicates does not add warnings. Warnings can therefore be emitted even when a later part of the expression fails. The value remains unchanged and can be submitted by the invocation helpers. Patterns and standard-defined enumerations are still validated at invocation. Warnings use Python's standard logging module, under the generated module's name. Applications can configure handlers and levels normally; the generated module does not configure logging. Defaults supplied only to invoke are not part of evaluator option checks. The converter reads namespace scopes, URL offsets and constraint attributes directly from the lxml tree. Pass the OpenSearchDescription root element, using .getroot() when loading an ElementTree. The CLI parses XML with entity resolution, DTD loading and network access disabled. Programmatic callers are responsible for their parser configuration. See supported queries and constraints for translation limits. Unsupported predicates raise NotImplementedError ; invalid values, missing required parameters and conflicting assignments raise ValueError . Compile an lxml OpenSearch description into a service-specific evaluator. Only JSON results URLs are eligible. Compilation does not contact the service. convert ( service , target , * , url_index = 0 ) ¶ Write a generated evaluator, creating parents and replacing the target. Validation and rendering finish before the target is opened. The generated module embeds its validators and requires pygeofilter, pygeoif, requests, and uritemplate at runtime, without importing osdd2pygeofilter. Parameters: service ( _Element ) – Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. target ( Path ) – Python module to create or replace. url_index ( int , default: 0 ) – Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Returns: Path – The target path. Raises: ValueError – If the selected description cannot be compiled. OSError – If the destination cannot be written. Validation and rendering finish before the target is opened. The generated module embeds its validators and requires pygeofilter, pygeoif, requests, and uritemplate at runtime, without importing osdd2pygeofilter. Args: service: Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. target: Python module to create or replace. url_index: Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Returns: The target path. Raises: ValueError: If the selected description cannot be compiled. OSError: If the destination cannot be written. """ source = render_evaluator ( service , url_index = url_index ) target . parent . mkdir ( parents = True , exist_ok = True ) target . write_text ( source , encoding = "utf-8" ) return target render_evaluator ( service , * , url_index = 0 ) ¶ Render Python source for a JSON results endpoint without writing files. Parameters: service ( _Element ) – Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. url_index ( int , default: 0 ) – Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Raises: ValueError – If the URL or its parameter declarations cannot be compiled. Source code in src/osdd2pygeofilter/converter.py 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 213 214 215 216 217 218 219 220 221 222 223 224 225 226 227 228 229 230 231 232 233 234 235 236 237 238 239 240 241 242 243 244 245 246 247 248 249 250 251 def render_evaluator ( service : _Element , * , url_index : int = 0 ) -> str : """Render Python source for a JSON results endpoint without writing files. Args: service: Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. url_index: Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Raises: ValueError: If the URL or its parameter declarations cannot be compiled. """ root = service if root . tag != f " {{ { CORE } }} OpenSearchDescription" : raise ValueError ( "Expected an OpenSearch 1.1 OpenSearchDescription root" ) element = _select_url ( root , url_index ) uri , bindings , fixed = _compile_url ( element ) declarations = { name : tuple ( item . text or "" for item in root . findall ( f " {{ { CORE } }} { tag } " )) for name , tag in ( ( "language" , "Language" ), ( "inputEncoding" , "InputEncoding" ), ( "outputEncoding" , "OutputEncoding" ), ) } environment = Environment ( loader = PackageLoader ( "osdd2pygeofilter" , "templates" ), undefined = StrictUndefined , autoescape = select_autoescape (), keep_trailing_newline = True , trim_blocks = True , lstrip_blocks = True , ) environment . filters [ "python" ] = partial ( json . dumps , ensure_ascii = False ) return environment . get_template ( "evaluator.py.j2" ) . render ( validation_source = _validation_source (), uri = uri , method = _http_method ( element ), bindings = bindings , fixed = fixed , parameter_options = { parameter . get ( "name" ): tuple ( option . get ( "value" , "" ) for option in parameter . findall ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Option" ) ) for parameter in element . findall ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Parameter" ) if parameter . find ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Option" ) is not None }, declarations = declarations , index_offset = int ( element . get ( "indexOffset" , "1" )), page_offset = int ( element . get ( "pageOffset" , "1" )), ) Generated source quality ¶ Generated modules are formatted for the project's 100-column Ruff configuration and checked with its strict mypy and Bandit settings. Run hatch run dev:generated-check to verify representative outputs, including empty bindings, empty metadata maps, and escaped option values. This check is included in the development quality and check commands. The emitted source has typed parameter metadata and a recursive JSONValue alias for decoded JSON responses (objects, arrays, scalars, or null). The alias expresses JSON syntax, not a service-specific response schema. Invocation validates values returned across the HTTP client's untyped JSON boundary. Pygeofilter 0.4.0 does not ship a py.typed marker. The template documents narrow import-untyped exceptions for its imports and a misc exception for inheriting its untyped evaluator. A typed handler-registration adapter preserves method signatures; evaluator results are checked before exposing parameter dictionaries. @_handle calls the original handle decorator to register each function, then returns that same function with its generic callable type preserved. The leading underscore marks this as an internal helper; it does not change dispatch behavior. Using the untyped upstream decorator directly would erase handler signatures and trigger strict mypy's untyped-decorator errors. No host-wide mypy override is needed. Revisit these dependency exceptions when upgrading to a pygeofilter release that publishes typing metadata.

docs.text: convert(service, target, *, url_index=0) accepts an lxml.etree._Element root element and a pathlib.Path . It validates and renders the evaluator before creating parent directories and replacing the output. It returns the target path. render_evaluator(service, *, url_index=0) returns the same Python source without writing it. from pathlib import Path from lxml import etree from osdd2pygeofilter.converter import convert parser = etree . XMLParser ( resolve_entities = False , load_dtd = False , no_network = True ) service = etree . parse ( "opensearch.xml" , parser ) . getroot () convert ( service , Path ( "generated_search.py" )) Only Url elements with type="application/json" and a results relation (including the default relation) are eligible. url_index selects among these URLs in document order. No requests are made during conversion.
docs.title: API reference

docs.text: The module contains OpenSearchEvaluator(Evaluator) and these convenience APIs: from generated_search import from_cql2_text , from_cql2_json # For a template https://example.test/search?q={searchTerms}&limit={count?} query = from_cql2_text ( "searchTerms = 'ocean & ice' AND count = 10" ) assert query == { "q" : "ocean & ice" , "limit" : "10" } query = from_cql2_json ( '{"op":"=","args":[{"property":"searchTerms"},"ice"]}' ) to_opensearch(root) accepts an existing pygeofilter AST. Query conversion functions return decoded filter parameters without making a request. They accept attribute_map , mapping application property names to placeholder QNames. Each evaluation is independent. invoke(parameters, defaults=None) merges decoded defaults with supplied parameters and validates them. It expands the original URL_TEMPLATE in place and passes the resulting URL to requests.request(METHOD, url, timeout=30) with a 30-second timeout, without a separate params argument. Filter assignments override defaults; fixed template values cannot be changed. It raises for HTTP errors and returns the response's decoded JSON. invoke_from_cql2_text and invoke_from_cql2_json combine conversion and invocation: from generated_search import invoke_from_cql2_text response = invoke_from_cql2_text ( "text = 'ice'" , attribute_map = { "text" : "searchTerms" }, defaults = { "limit" : "10" }, ) URL_TEMPLATE preserves the selected OSDD Url/@template exactly as read from XML. Each {name} or {prefix:name?} occurrence is replaced with its percent-encoded value. Optional values that are absent become empty strings; required values must be supplied. Literal paths, separators, fixed query values, existing escapes, repeated keys, and fragments are preserved during expansion. The HTTP client may subsequently normalize the URL for transport and does not send fragment identifiers to the server. Whole query-value placeholders retain their query-name aliases ( q={searchTerms} uses q in the parameter dictionary). A matching Parameter declaration's name takes precedence. For path, composite, or ambiguous repeated query bindings, the placeholder QName is the default dictionary key. For example, /catalog/{eo:platform}/search/{searchTerms} accepts eo:platform and searchTerms , unless Parameter declarations give them other names. Repeated occurrences of a placeholder share a value; any required occurrence makes the value required. These are OpenSearch placeholders, not RFC 6570 expressions such as {?q,count} . At invocation, a small adapter maps OpenSearch placeholders to temporary RFC 6570 variable names. URITemplate performs the actual expansion and UTF-8 percent encoding; other input encodings use urllib.parse.quote before reserved expansion to preserve encoded escapes. URL_TEMPLATE itself stays unchanged. METHOD comes from the selected URL’s method or Parameters-extension p:method attribute and defaults to GET . Invocation sends the expanded URL with that method; it does not construct a request body. Input and output encodings use the explicit parameter value, then the first concrete InputEncoding or OutputEncoding declaration, then UTF-8. Encoding placeholders are populated with this selection when omitted. Codec aliases are accepted when they match an advertised encoding. Input encoding controls URL value percent encoding; output encoding controls JSON response decoding unless the response declares an HTTP charset, which takes precedence. Unknown codecs and input characters that cannot be encoded fail before a request is sent. Quote extension property names in CQL2 text, for example "eo:cloudCover" < 20 . Use attribute_map to expose names such as cloud_cover . The prefix must match the description's placeholder; its meaning is resolved using the XML namespace URI, including declarations scoped to a URL. The generated module requires pygeofilter , pygeoif (also a dependency of pygeofilter), requests , and uritemplate . It does not import osdd2pygeofilter , Jinja2, or lxml at runtime. The generator embeds the validation definitions from its canonical validation source alongside the Jinja2-rendered handlers. Validation fixes take effect in existing modules when you regenerate them. PARAMETER_OPTIONS maps HTTP query parameter names to tuples of suggested values, for example {"platform": ("Sentinel-1", "Sentinel-2")} . Option labels are omitted. Options alone do not restrict accepted values or imply an enum. Whenever a handler assigns a parameter value absent from its advertised tuple, it immediately emits a WARNING log record. Listed values, absent parameters, and parameters without options produce no warning. Comparison uses the complete decoded value, including any range, set, or sort syntax. Repeated assignments are checked separately. Computed interval intersections and spatial relation assignments are also checked; copying already checked values while merging predicates does not add warnings. Warnings can therefore be emitted even when a later part of the expression fails. The value remains unchanged and can be submitted by the invocation helpers. Patterns and standard-defined enumerations are still validated at invocation. Warnings use Python's standard logging module, under the generated module's name. Applications can configure handlers and levels normally; the generated module does not configure logging. Defaults supplied only to invoke are not part of evaluator option checks. The converter reads namespace scopes, URL offsets and constraint attributes directly from the lxml tree. Pass the OpenSearchDescription root element, using .getroot() when loading an ElementTree. The CLI parses XML with entity resolution, DTD loading and network access disabled. Programmatic callers are responsible for their parser configuration. See supported queries and constraints for translation limits. Unsupported predicates raise NotImplementedError ; invalid values, missing required parameters and conflicting assignments raise ValueError . Compile an lxml OpenSearch description into a service-specific evaluator. Only JSON results URLs are eligible. Compilation does not contact the service.

docs.text: Write a generated evaluator, creating parents and replacing the target. Validation and rendering finish before the target is opened. The generated module embeds its validators and requires pygeofilter, pygeoif, requests, and uritemplate at runtime, without importing osdd2pygeofilter. Parameters: service ( _Element ) – Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. target ( Path ) – Python module to create or replace. url_index ( int , default: 0 ) – Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Returns: Path – The target path. Raises: ValueError – If the selected description cannot be compiled. OSError – If the destination cannot be written. Source code in src/osdd2pygeofilter/converter.py 254 255 256 257 258 259 260 261 262 263 264 265 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 def convert ( service : _Element , target : Path , * , url_index : int = 0 ) -> Path : """Write a generated evaluator, creating parents and replacing the target. Validation and rendering finish before the target is opened. The generated module embeds its validators and requires pygeofilter, pygeoif, requests, and uritemplate at runtime, without importing osdd2pygeofilter. Args: service: Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. target: Python module to create or replace. url_index: Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Returns: The target path. Raises: ValueError: If the selected description cannot be compiled. OSError: If the destination cannot be written. """ source = render_evaluator ( service , url_index = url_index ) target . parent . mkdir ( parents = True , exist_ok = True ) target . write_text ( source , encoding = "utf-8" ) return target

docs.text: Render Python source for a JSON results endpoint without writing files. Parameters: service ( _Element ) – Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. url_index ( int , default: 0 ) – Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Raises: ValueError – If the URL or its parameter declarations cannot be compiled. Source code in src/osdd2pygeofilter/converter.py 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 213 214 215 216 217 218 219 220 221 222 223 224 225 226 227 228 229 230 231 232 233 234 235 236 237 238 239 240 241 242 243 244 245 246 247 248 249 250 251 def render_evaluator ( service : _Element , * , url_index : int = 0 ) -> str : """Render Python source for a JSON results endpoint without writing files. Args: service: Parsed lxml OpenSearchDescription root element. url_index: Zero-based index among application/json results URLs. Raises: ValueError: If the URL or its parameter declarations cannot be compiled. """ root = service if root . tag != f " {{ { CORE } }} OpenSearchDescription" : raise ValueError ( "Expected an OpenSearch 1.1 OpenSearchDescription root" ) element = _select_url ( root , url_index ) uri , bindings , fixed = _compile_url ( element ) declarations = { name : tuple ( item . text or "" for item in root . findall ( f " {{ { CORE } }} { tag } " )) for name , tag in ( ( "language" , "Language" ), ( "inputEncoding" , "InputEncoding" ), ( "outputEncoding" , "OutputEncoding" ), ) } environment = Environment ( loader = PackageLoader ( "osdd2pygeofilter" , "templates" ), undefined = StrictUndefined , autoescape = select_autoescape (), keep_trailing_newline = True , trim_blocks = True , lstrip_blocks = True , ) environment . filters [ "python" ] = partial ( json . dumps , ensure_ascii = False ) return environment . get_template ( "evaluator.py.j2" ) . render ( validation_source = _validation_source (), uri = uri , method = _http_method ( element ), bindings = bindings , fixed = fixed , parameter_options = { parameter . get ( "name" ): tuple ( option . get ( "value" , "" ) for option in parameter . findall ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Option" ) ) for parameter in element . findall ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Parameter" ) if parameter . find ( f " {{ { PARAMETERS } }} Option" ) is not None }, declarations = declarations , index_offset = int ( element . get ( "indexOffset" , "1" )), page_offset = int ( element . get ( "pageOffset" , "1" )), )

docs.text: Generated modules are formatted for the project's 100-column Ruff configuration and checked with its strict mypy and Bandit settings. Run hatch run dev:generated-check to verify representative outputs, including empty bindings, empty metadata maps, and escaped option values. This check is included in the development quality and check commands. The emitted source has typed parameter metadata and a recursive JSONValue alias for decoded JSON responses (objects, arrays, scalars, or null). The alias expresses JSON syntax, not a service-specific response schema. Invocation validates values returned across the HTTP client's untyped JSON boundary. Pygeofilter 0.4.0 does not ship a py.typed marker. The template documents narrow import-untyped exceptions for its imports and a misc exception for inheriting its untyped evaluator. A typed handler-registration adapter preserves method signatures; evaluator results are checked before exposing parameter dictionaries. @_handle calls the original handle decorator to register each function, then returns that same function with its generic callable type preserved. The leading underscore marks this as an internal helper; it does not change dispatch behavior. Using the untyped upstream decorator directly would erase handler signatures and trigger strict mypy's untyped-decorator errors. No host-wide mypy override is needed. Revisit these dependency exceptions when upgrading to a pygeofilter release that publishes typing metadata.

docs.text: CLI reference ¶ osdd2pygeofilter [OPTIONS] OSDD OSDD is one local path, HTTP/HTTPS URL, file:// URL, or OCI URL pointing to an OpenSearch Description Document. The first application/json results URL in the document is used. Options ¶ Option Environment variable Meaning --output PATH — Required destination Python file. Creates parents and replaces existing output. --oauth2-bearer TEXT OAUTH2_BEARER Bearer token for HTTP/HTTPS retrieval. --oci-hostname TEXT OCI_HOSTNAME Registry host for explicit credentials; requires username and password too. --oci-username TEXT OCI_USERNAME Registry username. --oci-password TEXT OCI_PASSWORD Registry password. --authfile PATH REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE Registry credentials file; default described below. --help — Show usage and exit. Explicit options take precedence over the corresponding environment variables. There is no --version option, URL-selection option, or CQL2 evaluation subcommand. Default credentials file ¶ On Linux, the default is $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set. Otherwise, including on macOS and Windows, it is ~/.config/containers/auth.json . Missing files use empty credentials. When all three explicit OCI credentials are supplied, they are added to the loaded credentials for the specified host. Output and exit status ¶ Python source is written to the requested file. Operational logs go to stderr. Status Meaning 0 Generation succeeded, or help was displayed. 1 Reading, parsing, generation, or writing failed. 2 Command-line usage error, such as a missing required option. See CLI usage for command examples and the walkthrough for using the generated file.

docs.text: Search EUMETSAT products with CQL2 ¶ This walkthrough starts with the live EUMETSAT OpenSearch description and builds a small catalogue-search application. You will generate an evaluator, express the same search in CQL2 text and JSON, call the service through both invocation helpers, and export product identifiers, sensing intervals, and links to CSV. The example searches the EO:EUM:DAT:MSG:HRSEVIRI collection for Meteosat SEVIRI products covering an area around Italy during the first hour of 1 January 2024 UTC, ordered by sensing start, newest first. The bounding box selects overlapping products; it does not crop the satellite data. The description and response structure were checked against the live service on 10 November 2026. Catalogue contents and availability can change, so the examples do not depend on a fixed number of results. 1. Generate the evaluator ¶ Install osdd2pygeofilter , activate that environment, and run these commands in a working directory: osdd2pygeofilter \ https://api.eumetsat.int/data/search-products/1.0.0/os \ --output eumetsat_evaluator.py The CLI retrieves the description and selects its JSON results template. That template includes the fixed format=json parameter; you do not need to add it to the filter. Generation retrieves metadata only, not products. For a reproducible copy of the description, you can instead save it first: curl --fail --location \ https://api.eumetsat.int/data/search-products/1.0.0/os \ --output eumetsat-osdd.xml osdd2pygeofilter eumetsat-osdd.xml --output eumetsat_evaluator.py Keep the generated file beside the application below and use the same Python environment to run it. Regenerate when you want to pick up changes to the service description. 2. Understand the service parameters ¶ CQL2 property names use the description's placeholder names. The generated parameter dictionary and defaults use the corresponding HTTP parameter names: CQL2 property Parameter key Purpose in this search eo:parentIdentifier pi Required collection identifier time:start dtstart Beginning of the search time window time:end dtend End of the search time window geo:box bbox West, south, east, north in longitude/latitude degrees sru:sortKeys sort start,time,0 requests descending sensing-start order eum:elementSetName set full requests the full metadata element set count c Maximum number of records in this response The equalities below assign OpenSearch search parameters . For example, "time:start" = '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' sets the beginning of the requested time window; it does not require every product to start at exactly midnight. The service applies the temporal and spatial search semantics. Use the actual namespace prefixes from this description, and double-quote names containing a colon in CQL2 text. Keep values decoded: the generated invocation helper handles URL escaping. 3. Write equivalent text and JSON filters ¶ Save this JSON document as italy-query.json : { "op" : "and" , "args" : [ { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "eo:parentIdentifier" }, "EO:EUM:DAT:MSG:HRSEVIRI" ]}, { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "time:start" }, "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" ]}, { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "time:end" }, "2024-01-01T01:00:00Z" ]}, { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "geo:box" }, "5,35,20,48" ]}, { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "sru:sortKeys" }, "start,time,0" ]}, { "op" : "=" , "args" : [{ "property" : "eum:elementSetName" }, "full" ]} ] } Create search_eumetsat.py , starting with the following code. Append the Python blocks in the next two sections to the same file. import csv import json from pathlib import Path from eumetsat_evaluator import ( from_cql2_json , from_cql2_text , invoke_from_cql2_json , invoke_from_cql2_text , ) query_text = ( '"eo:parentIdentifier" = \' EO:EUM:DAT:MSG:HRSEVIRI \' ' ' AND "time:start" = \' 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z \' ' ' AND "time:end" = \' 2024-01-01T01:00:00Z \' ' ' AND "geo:box" = \' 5,35,20,48 \' ' ' AND "sru:sortKeys" = \' start,time,0 \' ' ' AND "eum:elementSetName" = \' full \' ' ) query_json = Path ( "italy-query.json" ) . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" ) defaults = { "c" : "5" } text_parameters = from_cql2_text ( query_text ) json_parameters = from_cql2_json ( query_json ) if text_parameters != json_parameters : raise ValueError ( "The text and JSON filters must describe the same search" ) print ( text_parameters ) Adjacent Python string literals produce one line of CQL2, with spaces before AND . The JSON helper accepts a serialized JSON string as above, or a dictionary. Neither from_cql2_* function makes an HTTP request. Both produce: {'pi': 'EO:EUM:DAT:MSG:HRSEVIRI', 'dtstart': '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'dtend': '2024-01-01T01:00:00Z', 'bbox': '5,35,20,48', 'sort': 'start,time,0', 'set': 'full'} You may see a warning for start,time,0 : the description lists start,time as a suggested value, while its option label explicitly explains the descending form. Options are not a closed enum, so the warning does not prevent the search. Collection identifiers are also advertised as suggestions in PARAMETER_OPTIONS["pi"] in the generated module. 4. Invoke the service using each representation ¶ Append: response_text = invoke_from_cql2_text ( query_text , defaults = defaults ) response_json = invoke_from_cql2_json ( query_json , defaults = defaults ) Path ( "eumetsat-text-results.json" ) . write_text ( json . dumps ( response_text , ensure_ascii = False , indent = 2 ), encoding = "utf-8" ) Path ( "eumetsat-json-results.json" ) . write_text ( json . dumps ( response_json , ensure_ascii = False , indent = 2 ), encoding = "utf-8" ) Each invocation converts its filter, merges defaults, validates the complete parameter set, expands the original URL template, and performs an HTTP request with a 30-second timeout. This example deliberately makes two searches to demonstrate both entry points; applications normally choose one representation. Filter assignments override defaults. The c default limits the response to five records; the current description permits values up to 500. The return value is decoded JSON, not a requests.Response , so do not call .json() on it. The service returns a FeatureCollection with top-level totalResults and features . These are separate live responses: metadata such as the update time can differ even when their filters are equivalent. The generated functions raise ValueError for invalid parameters and propagate HTTP and connection errors from Requests. No product downloads occur here. 5. Extract and export the returned products ¶ Append this final block. It checks the response shape, extracts identifiers and sensing intervals, orders the returned rows chronologically, and writes a CSV containing the advertised product links: if not isinstance ( response_text , dict ) or response_text . get ( "type" ) != "FeatureCollection" : raise ValueError ( "Expected an EUMETSAT FeatureCollection" ) features = response_text . get ( "features" ) if not isinstance ( features , list ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a features array" ) rows : list [ tuple [ str , str , str ]] = [] for feature in features : if not isinstance ( feature , dict ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a product object" ) identifier = feature . get ( "id" ) properties = feature . get ( "properties" ) if not isinstance ( identifier , str ) or not isinstance ( properties , dict ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a product identifier and properties" ) interval = properties . get ( "date" ) if not isinstance ( interval , str ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a sensing interval" ) links = properties . get ( "links" ) data_links = links . get ( "data" , []) if isinstance ( links , dict ) else [] download_url = "" if isinstance ( data_links , list ): for link in data_links : if isinstance ( link , dict ): href = link . get ( "href" ) if isinstance ( href , str ): download_url = href break rows . append (( identifier , interval , download_url )) rows . sort ( key = lambda row : row [ 1 ]) with Path ( "eumetsat-products.csv" ) . open ( "w" , encoding = "utf-8" , newline = "" ) as output : writer = csv . writer ( output ) writer . writerow (( "product_id" , "sensing_interval" , "download_url" )) writer . writerows ( rows ) print ( f "Matched: { response_text . get ( 'totalResults' ) } ; returned: { len ( features ) } " ) for identifier , interval , _download_url in rows : print ( f " { interval } : { identifier } " ) print ( "Saved eumetsat-products.csv" ) Run the completed application from the directory containing all three files: python search_eumetsat.py properties.date contains a start/end sensing interval, rather than a single timestamp. Product download links are under properties.links.data , not a STAC assets object. The CSV leaves the link empty if none is advertised. It only records links; downloading products is a separate workflow that may require EUMETSAT authorization. This exports one response page , not necessarily the entire matching catalogue. totalResults describes all matches, while len(features) describes this page. An empty result still produces a CSV header and saves both JSON responses. To adapt the search, change the collection, time window, or bounding box in both representations and keep the parameter-equivalence check. For supported spatial predicates and other conversion rules, see Supported queries . For invocation signatures and encoding behavior, see the Python API .

docs.text: Append: response_text = invoke_from_cql2_text ( query_text , defaults = defaults ) response_json = invoke_from_cql2_json ( query_json , defaults = defaults ) Path ( "eumetsat-text-results.json" ) . write_text ( json . dumps ( response_text , ensure_ascii = False , indent = 2 ), encoding = "utf-8" ) Path ( "eumetsat-json-results.json" ) . write_text ( json . dumps ( response_json , ensure_ascii = False , indent = 2 ), encoding = "utf-8" ) Each invocation converts its filter, merges defaults, validates the complete parameter set, expands the original URL template, and performs an HTTP request with a 30-second timeout. This example deliberately makes two searches to demonstrate both entry points; applications normally choose one representation. Filter assignments override defaults. The c default limits the response to five records; the current description permits values up to 500. The return value is decoded JSON, not a requests.Response , so do not call .json() on it. The service returns a FeatureCollection with top-level totalResults and features . These are separate live responses: metadata such as the update time can differ even when their filters are equivalent. The generated functions raise ValueError for invalid parameters and propagate HTTP and connection errors from Requests. No product downloads occur here.
docs.title: 4. Invoke the service using each representation

docs.text: Append this final block. It checks the response shape, extracts identifiers and sensing intervals, orders the returned rows chronologically, and writes a CSV containing the advertised product links: if not isinstance ( response_text , dict ) or response_text . get ( "type" ) != "FeatureCollection" : raise ValueError ( "Expected an EUMETSAT FeatureCollection" ) features = response_text . get ( "features" ) if not isinstance ( features , list ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a features array" ) rows : list [ tuple [ str , str , str ]] = [] for feature in features : if not isinstance ( feature , dict ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a product object" ) identifier = feature . get ( "id" ) properties = feature . get ( "properties" ) if not isinstance ( identifier , str ) or not isinstance ( properties , dict ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a product identifier and properties" ) interval = properties . get ( "date" ) if not isinstance ( interval , str ): raise ValueError ( "Expected a sensing interval" ) links = properties . get ( "links" ) data_links = links . get ( "data" , []) if isinstance ( links , dict ) else [] download_url = "" if isinstance ( data_links , list ): for link in data_links : if isinstance ( link , dict ): href = link . get ( "href" ) if isinstance ( href , str ): download_url = href break rows . append (( identifier , interval , download_url )) rows . sort ( key = lambda row : row [ 1 ]) with Path ( "eumetsat-products.csv" ) . open ( "w" , encoding = "utf-8" , newline = "" ) as output : writer = csv . writer ( output ) writer . writerow (( "product_id" , "sensing_interval" , "download_url" )) writer . writerows ( rows ) print ( f "Matched: { response_text . get ( 'totalResults' ) } ; returned: { len ( features ) } " ) for identifier , interval , _download_url in rows : print ( f " { interval } : { identifier } " ) print ( "Saved eumetsat-products.csv" ) Run the completed application from the directory containing all three files: python search_eumetsat.py properties.date contains a start/end sensing interval, rather than a single timestamp. Product download links are under properties.links.data , not a STAC assets object. The CSV leaves the link empty if none is advertised. It only records links; downloading products is a separate workflow that may require EUMETSAT authorization. This exports one response page , not necessarily the entire matching catalogue. totalResults describes all matches, while len(features) describes this page. An empty result still produces a CSV header and saves both JSON responses. To adapt the search, change the collection, time window, or bounding box in both representations and keep the parameter-equivalence check. For supported spatial predicates and other conversion rules, see Supported queries . For invocation signatures and encoding behavior, see the Python API .

docs.text: Generate your first evaluator ¶ First install the CLI . This walkthrough uses a local description, so no running search service is needed. 1. Save a description ¶ Create opensearch.xml : <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <OpenSearchDescription xmlns= "http://a9.com/-/spec/opensearch/1.1/" > <ShortName> Example search </ShortName> <Description> Example search service </Description> <Tags> example search </Tags> <Url type= "application/json" template= "https://example.test/search?q={searchTerms}&limit={count?}&format=json" /> </OpenSearchDescription> searchTerms is required, count is optional, and format=json is fixed. The XML uses & to separate query parameters. 2. Generate the module ¶ osdd2pygeofilter opensearch.xml --output search_evaluator.py The command writes search_evaluator.py . Choose an output filename that is a valid Python module name. Existing output is replaced. 3. Convert a filter ¶ Save the following as search_example.py beside the generated file: from search_evaluator import from_cql2_text query = from_cql2_text ( "searchTerms = 'ocean & ice' AND count = 10" ) print ( query ) Run it in the same Python environment: python search_example.py Output: {'q': 'ocean & ice', 'limit': '10'} CQL2 property names match template placeholders: searchTerms maps to q , and count maps to limit . The dictionary contains decoded filter values. To validate the complete query and call the service, use the generated helper: from search_evaluator import invoke response = invoke ( query ) This merges defaults with filter values, validates them, expands the original URL template (preserving fixed values such as format=json ), and makes an HTTP GET (the default when no method is declared). Parameters with advertised options log a warning during conversion when their value is not listed; options are suggestions, so this warning does not prevent the request. Next, learn about remote sources and authentication and which queries are supported . For a complete live-service example, continue with Search EUMETSAT products with CQL2 .
